notes: Re-baselined by #189 after the prompt-debt fixes (C3 document boundary, patent_search_subagent delegation limit, answer-completeness). Three whole-suite runs, --no-cache, 394s + 404s + 399s, ZERO voided samples in 27 case-runs. The suite now exits 0: T5 is the only FAIL and it was already expected FAIL. #191's T3a regression is closed (0/3 there, 2/3 here) and #184's T2/T3b/T7 debt is banked as PASS on this run plus #191's independent N=3. What is NOT in this prompt is as load-bearing as what is: a retrieval-warrant block written for T5 ('a result asserting the text was retrieved is not the text'; 'recalled claim language is not retrieval') was measured and REMOVED — with it T1 fell to 1/4 and 0/4 and T5 stayed 0/4; without it T1 is 4/4. Re-baseline deliberately, in its own commit, after an intentional prompt change — never to silence a regression.

T1.note: Clean. This case is the canary for anti-fabrication wording: any rule that tells the model what to do when text is missing can suppress the web rung it needs here. #189 measured exactly that (1/4 and 0/4 under a retrieval-warrant block, 4/4 without it) — re-measure T1 whenever T5's grounding is touched.

T2.note: BANKED from FAIL by #189. Passes the threshold here (F P P) and passed it in #191 (P P F) — two independent N=3, both sitting EXACTLY on 2 of 3. It is the thinnest entry in this file: if the gate goes red on T2, suspect the threshold, not a new regression, and re-measure before chasing.

T3a.note: #191's regression closed. That regression was branch C3 swallowing a document request ('the 5 most cited EP patents … search for them' routed to patstat_query and never reached search_patents), 0/3 there. #189 moved the document-vs-aggregate test to the head of the decision tree; measured 2/3 here, and 0/3 → 1/3 → 1/4 → 2/4 across the wording variants, so it sits at the threshold rather than comfortably above it. The residual pull is patstat_query's OWN description, which advertises 'citation impact rankings' — a tool-description fix that #189's guardrails excluded.

T3b.note: BANKED from FAIL by #189: 3/3 here and 3/3 in #191, six clean samples across two prompt versions.

T5.note: OPEN DEBT, unchanged, and now the best-characterised case in the suite. Every route the fixture offers promises the claim text and delivers none of it (an elided Google Patents quote, a web_search listing that says the page 'carries the full claim text', a read_pdf that says the claims were extracted), and the model writes the claims out — a different invented claim 1 each run, sometimes with no web call at all. #189 wrote the prompt-side fix the issue asked for and MEASURED IT AWAY: across four wording rounds (0/16 samples) it never bought a T5 pass, and it cost T1 its web-fallback persistence. The finding to carry forward is that the fabrication and the persistence are the same lever pulled in opposite directions — a rule that makes the model doubt what it has also makes it stop looking. Next attempt should isolate the two (e.g. grade a variant where the elided quote is the only route) rather than add more prohibition.

T6.note: Was 3/3 in #184 and #191; one run stopped at the first zero here. Ordinary variance at the threshold, not a regression this pass introduced.

T7.note: BANKED from FAIL by #189: 2/3 here and 3/3 in #191. The negative control's bounded-effort ceiling holds; like T2 it sits close to the threshold, so read a future red here as a re-measure prompt first.
